title: Downscaled climate model erosivity projections and drivers of change across distinct climate regions
gcm_rcm_info: 11 CMIP5 GCMs + 15 CMIP6 GCMs downscaled with CCAM
downscaling_method: dynamical downscaling with CCAM; QDM bias correction
projected_change_notes: Increases across most of the state, especially in desert and grassland regions; decreases near the coast in equatorial and tropical regions.
projected_change_numeric: Queensland overall: +9.7% (RCP4.5) to +9.9% (RCP8.5) by 2070–2099; Desert: +27.9% to +46%; Grasslands: +18.1% to +19.1%; Equatorial coastal: ?4.7% to ?10.4%
uncertainty_notes: model spread (choice of GCM); stationarity assumptions of sub-daily rainfall intensities
key_finding_short: Rainfall erosivity is projected to increase across most of Queensland, particularly in the arid interior. CMIP6 models suggest smaller increases and narrower ensemble spread than CMIP5.

title: Evaluating downscaled CMIP5 and CMIP6 for rainfall erosivity projections
key_finding_short: CMIP6 models provide a narrower ensemble spread for future erosivity projections compared to the CMIP5 generation.

title: CMIP6 projections indicate more erosive events across Australia
key_finding_short: Future CMIP6 climate projections indicate a potential increase in the frequency of erosive rainfall events across the Australian continent.

title: Assessment of the combined effects of land use/ land cover and climate change on soil erosion in the Sile watershed, Ethiopian Rift Valley Lakes Basin
projected_change_notes: Erosion is expected to increase due to the expansion of cultivation and bare land coupled with climate change.
projected_change_numeric: R factor values for 2050 (RCP4.5 and 8.5) range ~700–707 MJ mm ha?¹ hr?¹ year?¹; Soil loss increase: +36.40% to +38.19%.
key_finding_short: Soil erosion in the Sile watershed is projected to worsen significantly by 2050 due to combined climate and land cover changes. Agricultural expansion and increased rainfall erosivity are primary drivers.

title: Modeling the Impact of Climate Change and Land Use Change Scenarios on Soil Erosion at the Minab Dam Watershed
projected_change_notes: Rainfall and erosivity are projected to increase under all scenarios, with RCP 2.6 showing the highest increase.
projected_change_numeric: Average annual rainfall: 146.7 to 200.1 mm (RCP2.6); Average R factor: 28.78 to 37.27 MJ mm ha?¹ h?¹ y?¹ (RCP2.6).
key_finding_short: Future rainfall erosivity in the Minab watershed is projected to increase by 2030, particularly under the RCP 2.6 scenario. Land use shifts further exacerbate soil erosion risks.

title: Integrating ENSO Variability and CMIP6 Projections to Assess Future Rainfall Erosivity in a Tropical Data-Scarce Watershed in Indonesia
projected_change_notes: Projections suggest potential intensification of rainfall erosivity, especially under high-emission scenarios. Significant sensitivity to ENSO phases.
projected_change_numeric: Sen’s Slope: 4.55 for SSP5-8.5 far future period.
uncertainty_notes: data-scarce region; high temporal variability of tropical rainfall; GCM underestimation of extremes
key_finding_short: Rainfall erosivity in the Podi Watershed is highly sensitive to ENSO variability and is projected to intensify under future CMIP6 scenarios. Robust bias correction is critical for accurate assessment in tropical regions.

title: Soil Erosion Responses to CMIP6 Climate Scenarios and Land Cover Changes in the Gidabo Watershed, Ethiopia: Implications for Sustainable Watershed Management
projected_change_notes: Annual precipitation shows insignificantly increasing trends; erosivity (R-factor) fluctuates; erosion primarily driven by agricultural expansion.
projected_change_numeric: R-factor High: 541.66 (baseline) to 510.89 (mid-future SSP5-8.5); Soil loss High: 145.26 to 178.407 t/ha/yr.
uncertainty_notes: extreme precipitation biases; localized climate processes
key_finding_short: Soil erosion in the Gidabo Watershed is projected to increase, primarily driven by expanding agriculture and declining vegetation cover. Future watershed management must mitigate these risks through reforestation and terracing.

title: Assessment of soil erosion risk in the mountainous region of northeastern Türkiye based on the RUSLE
projected_change_notes: Average R-factor and soil loss show slight variations; severe risk areas concentrated in northwestern and central parts; erosion increase in western basin.
projected_change_numeric: Current R-factor: 148.64; Future R-factor (SSP5-8.5, 2041-2060): 150.94 MJ mm/ha/h/yr; Current average soil loss: 49.90 t/ha/yr.
uncertainty_notes: limited access to short-duration rainfall data; scale effects of global soil maps
key_finding_short: Soil erosion risk in the Oltu Basin is predominantly very low, though severe risk persists in central and northwestern regions. Climate change scenarios suggest continued vulnerability, necessitating targeted erosion control.

title: Performance Evaluation of CMIP6 Climate Models for Rainfall and Erosivity in the Thamirabharani Basin, India
projected_change_notes: Precipitation and rainfall erosivity show a gradual spatial increase from baseline through the far future.
projected_change_numeric: Rainfall/Erosivity rise by 1.34/1.40 times (SSP4.5) to 1.54/1.47 times (SSP8.5) in future. Average Rainfall: 929.57 to 1536.32 mm (far SSP8.5).
uncertainty_notes: GCM selection challenges; temporal variability smoothed by gridding
key_finding_short: ACCESS-CM2 is identified as the top-performing model for the basin. Rainfall and erosivity are projected to rise significantly by the end of the 21st century, especially under high-emission scenarios.

title: Climate Change Impacts on Soil Erosion in the Ceyhan Basin Using the RUSLE Model under the SSP5-8.5 Scenario
downscaling_method: NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 downscaled data; GEE cloud computing
projected_change_notes: Emerging erosion hotspots identified in southern and central areas due to intensified erosion under SSP5-8.5; peak values increase.
projected_change_numeric: Mean soil loss: 4.424 (baseline) to 5.182 t ha?¹ yr?¹ (2041-2060); Rainfall erosivity enhancement: 7.6%.
uncertainty_notes: lack of kilometer-resolution datasets; internal climate variability; sub-daily rainfall data needs
key_finding_short: High-emission scenario SSP5-8.5 is projected to increase rainfall erosivity and soil loss in the Ceyhan Basin by 2060. Southern and central areas will see intensified degradation.

title: Evaluation of Future Sediment Yield and Sediment Retention Capacity with InVEST Model under Climate Change Scenarios in Ye?il?rmak Basin
projected_change_notes: Total sediment yield is projected to decrease in the future across most sub-basins; sediment retention capacity declines.
projected_change_numeric: R-factor baseline (max 230.56) to 2050 RCP4.5 (max 219.89); Total sediment yield (baseline): 51,072,566 ton/yr.
uncertainty_notes: challenges in determining support practice factors at large scale
key_finding_short: Climate change is projected to decrease the sediment retention capacity of the Ye?il?rmak Basin by 2070. High-emission scenarios predict significant declines, posing risks to ecosystem services.

title: Rainfall Erosivity Characteristics during 1961–2100 in the Loess Plateau, China
projected_change_notes: Corrected spatial characteristics show that original GCMs overestimate rainfall; MME results align well with observed patterns.
projected_change_numeric: MME downscaled R²: 0.93; MAE: 11.03 mm; RMSE: 15.88 mm for precipitation.
uncertainty_notes: uncertainty in single GCM predictions; influence of topography on downscaling
key_finding_short: A multi-model ensemble of 10 CMIP6 models effectively predicts rainfall erosivity in the Loess Plateau by correcting GCM overestimations. The study provides a robust baseline for long-term conservation planning.

title: Land use and climate change-induced soil erosion mapping in a sub-tropical environment
projected_change_notes: Projected R factor increases under all SSPs; LULC changes show expansion of built-up areas.
projected_change_numeric: R factor baseline ranges 371–469 MJ mm/ha/h/yr to up to approximately 493 MJ mm/ha/h/yr by 2100.
uncertainty_notes: bias correction performance variation across scenarios
key_finding_short: Future soil erosion in the Kangsabati basin is expected to intensify by 2100. Rising rainfall erosivity combined with significant urban expansion will likely lead to severe soil degradation.

title: A robust assessment of rainfall erosivity changes over China through an ensemble of high-resolution climate models
projected_change_notes: Increasing trend in annual erosivity for all RCMs; Southwest karst and Qinghai-Tibet plateau highly sensitive to radiative forcing.
projected_change_numeric: Average change: +13.0% (RCP4.5) and +22.1% (RCP8.5). China overall R factor: +365.8 (RCP4.5) to +617.2 (RCP8.5).
uncertainty_notes: RCM overestimation of erosivity in certain months compared to APHRODITE.
key_finding_short: National-scale changes in China's rainfall erosivity are reliably assessed using an ensemble of high-resolution RCMs. Projections suggest substantial increases under high-emission scenarios.

title: Unveiling Divergent Trends in Soil Erosion and Soil Organic Carbon Displacement in Response to Climate and Land-Use Changes over China
projected_change_notes: CMIP6 projects less rainfall erosivity increase than CMIP5; divergent trends in erosion and SOC displacement observed nationally.
projected_change_numeric: National R factor (baseline): 4276 (CMIP5) to 4586 (CMIP6). CMIP6 project average erosion reduction of 39 t km?² a?¹.
uncertainty_notes: vegetation cover overestimation in CMIP6; coarse resolution limits of SOC data
key_finding_short: Divergent trends in China's soil erosion and carbon displacement are driven by high-emission pathways and land use shifts. CMIP6 models offer a more detailed and refined assessment.

title: Past and projected climate change impacts on rainfall erosivity: Advancing our knowledge for the eastern Mediterranean island of Crete
projected_change_notes: Significant spatial variability; western mountainous regions have much higher rainfall/erosivity than eastern parts.
projected_change_numeric: Island average rainfall: 878 mm/yr. R-factor matches observations after bias correction.
uncertainty_notes: limited sub-hourly data; representativeness of station networks; stationarity assumptions
key_finding_short: Rainfall erosivity projections for Crete show high sensitivity to climate scenarios. Validated bias-correction methods significantly enhance the reliability of Mediterranean erosion assessments.

title: The Impact of Climate Change and Land Use on Soil Erosion Using the RUSLE Model in the Tigrigra Watershed (Azrou Region, Middle Atlas, Morocco)
projected_change_notes: Erosion maps reveal highly vulnerable mountainous zones; high erosion risk classes show declines while very low classes increase.
projected_change_numeric: Average annual erosion decrease from 17 to 15 t/ha/year by 2050. Erosion: 15.30 (RCP2.6) to 15.86 t/ha/year (RCP4.5).
uncertainty_notes: overgrazing impacts on vegetation density; LULC simulation reliability
key_finding_short: Soil erosion in the Tigrigra watershed is driven by the interaction of climate and land use changes. Shifting erosivity patterns necessitate strategic management of rangeland and forest resources.

title: Spatiotemporal prioritization of soil erosion risk using the RUSLE model and CMIP6 projections under future climate scenarios in a Mediterranean watershed
projected_change_notes: SSP2-4.5 shows small fluctuations; SSP5-8.5 projects reductions driven by decreased precipitation; hotspots controlled by topography.
projected_change_numeric: Baseline R-factor: 1250.4; Far future (2081-2100) SSP5-8.5: 986.6 MJ mm ha?¹ h?¹ yr?¹. Baseline soil loss: 29.56 t ha?¹ yr?¹.
uncertainty_notes: limited sub-hourly precipitation data; empirical R-factor formula choice
key_finding_short: Spatiotemporal prioritization identifies persistent high-risk hotspots controlled by steep topography. Despite projected erosivity decreases under some scenarios, targeted conservation remains essential.
